findings.title: [P1] Validate post-login redirects before navigation
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from a login parameter, an attacker can supply an external or `javascript:` URL. Passing it directly to `location.assign` enables post-login phishing and, where permitted, script execution in the application context. Accept only validated same-origin HTTP(S) paths.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to application logs
findings.body: Every issued token is passed to `audit`, whose new implementation writes the complete value to `console.log`. Log collectors and support personnel could recover these bearer credentials and impersonate users until expiration or revocation. Record non-sensitive metadata instead.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict the post-login navigation to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
Passing an attacker-controlled absolute or protocol-relative `returnUrl` (for example, `https://evil.example`) now redirects authenticated users off-site instead of always transitioning to `/dashboard`, introducing an open redirect usable in phishing flows.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to application logs
findings.body:
Every call records the full token via `console.log`. Where console output is collected or accessible to support personnel, any valid bearer token can be recovered and used to impersonate its holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin paths
findings.body:
`location.assign` accepts absolute and protocol URLs. If `returnUrl` is derived from a login/query parameter, values such as `https://attacker.example` create an open redirect; permissive environments may also execute `javascript:` URLs.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restrict login redirects to trusted HTTP(S) destinations
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` is attacker-controlled, values such as `javascript:...` can execute script in the application context where permitted; external URLs also enable post-login phishing redirects. Validate the scheme and enforce an allowlist or same-origin relative paths.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every invocation records the complete token through `console.log`. In environments where console output is retained or aggregated, anyone with log access can recover bearer credentials and impersonate users until those tokens expire or are revoked.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
